newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-BENTLEY WINS LIONS TEST CALL.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-BENTLEY WINS LIONS TEST CALL.

text.p: Winger John Bentley will bridge a nine-year gap when he makes his debut for the British Lions in the second test against South Africa in Durban on Saturday.
The 30-year-old was called up on Thursday to replace injured Ieuan Evans in the only change from the side who won the first test 25-16 in Cape Town last weekend.

It reopens a remarkable chapter in Bentley's international rugby union career which appeared to be over when he signed for Leeds rugby league club in 1988 after winning his two rugby union caps for England earlier that year.
"He is obviously not one of the youngest members of the party but he is now coming into it like a new player," said coach Ian McGeechan.
"These are new challenges for him in his career which he did not necessarily expect."
Bentley returned to rugby union last year with Newcastle which shares him with the Halifax rugby league club.

He was overlooked by the England selectors for this year's Five Nations but was one of the surprise choices for the Lions. His ebullient character and try-scoring form -- he is the leading Lions scorer with seven tries in six matches -- have justifed the selectors' boldness.
Manager Fran Cotton admitted Bentley might have forced his way into the team even if Evans had been fit.
"It was a difficult selection process which took far longer than we would have expected having won the first test," said Cotton.
"There was a lot of debate about four or five positions."
Irish number eight Eric Miller, who was unavailable with flu for the first test, has been added to the replacements after pushing Tim Rodber close for the position at the base of the scrum.
Neil Back, the pocket battleship English flanker, also gains a place on the replacements bench which features four forwards and English half-backs Austin Healey and Michael Catt.
McGeechan said: "The first test is always a new experience for both sides but for the second both sides will be up to speed and very often you see a different style of rugby.
"There's no doubt the intensity and pace will be up on Newlands."
The third and final test is in Johannesburg on July 5.

British Lions - 15-Neil Jenkins; 14-John Bentley, 13-Jeremy Guscott, 12-Scott Gibbs, 11-Allan Tait; 10-Gregor Townsend, 9-Matt Dawson; 8-Tim Rodber, 7-Richard Hill, 6-Lawrence Dallaglio, 5-Jeremy Davidson, 4-Martin Johnson (captain), 3-Paul Wallace, 2-Keith Wood, 1-Tom Smith.
Replacements: Neil Back, Mike Catt, Austin Healey, Barry Williams, Jason Leonard, Eric Miller.
